newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Buyer bowls over Sotheby's with porcelain bid.
newsitem.headline: Buyer bowls over Sotheby's with porcelain bid.

text.p: A British buyer bowled over auctioneers in Hong Kong on Tuesday by bidding a record HK$21.47 million (US$2.77 million) for a piece of Chinese Qing dynasty porcelain.
The Imperial yellow-ground bowl decorated with puce landscapes of hills and pavilions was bought by London dealer Eskenazi Ltd, auction house Sotheby's said in a statement.
The price was the highest ever paid for a porcelain piece dating from the Qing dynasty, which ruled China from 1644-1911, the company said.
The bowl was one of nine pieces of porcelain that sold for a total of HK$80.42 million, among the highest prices paid for Imperial porcelain in many years, it said.
